For destination calendars without credentialId (legacy path, EventManager.ts:370-375), EventManager writes externalCalendarId: result.externalId === undefined into the BookingReference; on later update/delete, GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent/deleteEvent hit the dead fallback (finding 1) or pass calendarId undefined, so those events can never be moved or removed — remote calendar data is silently orphaned on reschedule/cancel.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes CalendarManager.createEvent return `{ externalId }` from its third argument (added param `externalId?: string`) without deriving it from the provider result, and EventManager now persists booking references using `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` (EventManager.ts around the two places setting `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`). In `createAllCalendarEvents`, the no-`credentialId` branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`, so `result.externalId` is `undefined` even though the destination calendar may have an `externalId` (EventManager.ts loop: `destinationCalendarCredentials.map(async (c) => await createEvent(c, event))`). That means references can be written with `externalCalendarId` undefined. Later, GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent/deleteEvent rely on `externalCalendarId` to choose a calendarId, but the new fallback is effectively dead (`event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` when `externalCalendarId` is null/undefined), so the calendarId can stay undefined, breaking update/delete and potentially orphaning remote events.
